headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure from residential users to large energy users, primarily data centers, to reduce residential utility bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, U.S. Sen. Mark Warner (co-sponsored similar federal legislation).
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users, Dominion Energy (initially).
news_headline: Governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers. Critics say her tweaks weaken them. Don't believe it.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed HB 1393, which aims to shift electricity costs to data centers, but her amendments replaced a direct requirement for data centers to cover capacity market costs with more regulatory authority for the SCC to allocate costs. Despite criticism that these tweaks weaken the bill, proponents argue they will still save money for residential customers by restricting Dominion's spending and capping its return on equity.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates data centers to report their water usage, providing transparency and data for future water management policies and environmental monitoring.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local governments, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (potential administrative burden, privacy concerns).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, with the numbers to be aggregated and made available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website by January 1, 2027. This transparency measure, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, aims to address concerns about data centers' significant water consumption and provide credible data for water management.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes guidelines for where data centers can be built and sets limits on the noise they can produce, addressing community concerns about quality of life.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: Virginia, home to hundreds of data centers, adds new restrictions
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed bills, including HB 153, to regulate data centers, addressing concerns about noise and siting. This legislation introduces new siting requirements for large data centers, mandating impact assessments on agriculture, parks, and historical sites before rezoning approval, and aims to mitigate community impacts and preserve quality of life.
